title: Triangle covering-to-packing ratio
formal: Determine \(\Gamma _{\triangle}=\sup\){\(\tau _{\triangle}(G)/\nu _{\triangle}(G): G\) is a finite simple undirected graph with at least one triangle}, where \(\tau _{\triangle}\) and \(\nu _{\triangle}\) are defined below.
definitions: A simple graph has no loops or parallel edges. A triangle is a set of three distinct vertices together with all three edges between them. An edge set F meets every triangle if each triangle contains at least one edge of F; equivalently, deleting F makes G triangle-free. Define \(\tau _{\triangle}\) as the minimum cardinality of such \(F\subseteq E(G)\). A packing is a family of triangles whose three-edge sets are pairwise disjoint; triangles in a packing may share vertices. Define \(\nu _{\triangle}\) as the maximum cardinality of a packing. Both values are zero when G has no triangles, including the empty graph. The inequality concerns integral edge sets and integral packings, with no fractional weights and no running-time requirement. Restricting the ratio to graphs containing a triangle avoids a zero denominator; triangle-free graphs already satisfy every nonnegative-factor comparison. The supremum is finite: deleting every edge of a maximal triangle packing gives \(\tau _{\triangle}\le 3\nu _{\triangle}\). Attainment of the supremum is not required.
answer_criterion: Supply a specified real number a and prove in Lean that |\(a- \Gamma _{\triangle}|\le 1/100\). The proof must certify both a lower and an upper bound for the unrestricted quantity in this card. Equivalently, certified bounds \(\ell\)\(\le u\) of width at most \(1/50\) qualify by taking \(a=(\ell +u)/2\). An exact value with proof of equality also qualifies. An unevaluated copy of the defining extremum, a one-sided improvement, or a numerical estimate without a proved error bound does not meet this criterion. The \(1/100\) tolerance is benchmark acceptance; it does not prove an associated exact threshold conjecture.
why: Establish the proposed sharp factor-two relation between destroying all triangles and packing disjoint triangles.

importance.reason: A fundamental integral packing-versus-covering problem tied to two canonical graph optimization tasks.

context_blocks.text: The target is the best universal covering-to-packing factor. Tuza’s conjecture gives the candidate \(\Gamma _{\triangle}=2\), but the quantitative question also asks for the value if that conjecture fails.

A triangle packing exhibits many separate obstructions to triangle-freeness. An edge cover removes all such obstructions. Every cover must meet each member of a packing, while taking all edges of a maximal packing gives the elementary factor-three comparison.

Tuza asks whether the covering cost always stays within twice the maximum packing size. Edge-disjointness is essential: the triangles may meet at vertices. The four-vertex complete graph has packing number one and covering number two, so a smaller universal factor is impossible.

Results for dense or bounded-degree graphs and fractional relaxations do not establish the integral inequality for arbitrary graphs. The August 2026 degree-seven manuscript is recorded as a preprint claim rather than an independently verified proof.

sentences: Triangle covering deletes edges to eliminate every triangle, while triangle packing selects edge-disjoint triangles.
The target is the supremum ratio of these two integral optima over finite simple graphs with a triangle.
Packed triangles may share vertices but cannot share edges.
Tuza’s conjecture predicts that the universal ratio equals two.
The numerical benchmark requires a Lean-certified value within absolute error 0.01.
